reasons.dead|div#mapMode: the map is the operating table and the tour control is a strip docked at its top-left corner; the space under the strip is the map the strip drives, and the map is the subject of the page, not a gap in it.
reasons.dead|div#satHud: the scope panel is docked at the map's top-right corner, over the territory it counts; the space under the panel is that territory, and the panel is the only thing in the hero that says what is in view.
reasons.dead|div#heroCityLabel: the city name is painted onto the map canvas; the element is a one-pixel anchor for that name, so the space around it is the map the name is written on.
reasons.dead|div.hero-map-space: on a phone the map runs full-bleed behind the headline, so this spacer holds the map's height and the headline begins below the map instead of over it.
reasons.dead|div.hero-proof: the decision console is the last block in the hero's right column, and the three figures under it are the page's own summary row; the space under the console is the gap between the console and those figures.
reasons.dead|span.field-band__point-num: the number is a hanging marker in the margin of the paragraph it numbers; the paragraph's own text fills that column, so the space under the marker is the paragraph, not a hole.
reasons.dead|div.sys-cell__head: the space under the card head is the system's own screenshot, always 21:8, so every catalogue card is the same height and a row of cards reads as one row rather than as a staircase.
reasons.scattered|div#heroNodeRail: the four theatre cards are one row of a four-column grid, all four visible at once because they are the same kind of choice — which theatre to watch — and the active one is marked.
reasons.dead|aside#caseStudyList: the list is a selector, not a column of content: it holds three records and the record's own fifteen fields run far below them, so the rail ends where its records end. The rail is sticky, so it follows the reader down the form.
reasons.wrap|div.probono-stack: The shelf lists the technologies each pro bono project was built on — four names in a card 239px wide. The line falls where the names run out of room and the last line holds whatever is left over. A technology name is not an option, an action or a control, so nothing the reader is hunting for is stranded on that line. The layout before this was a two-column grid whose track every chip stretched into: “D1”, twelve pixels of text, sat in a 167px cell at 390px and a 108px cell at 1440 — twelve times its own width. A lone final name is the end of a list; a chip inflated to twelve times its name is a lie about the name.
reasons.wrap|div.stack__items: The shelf is the full technology stack — 114 names in nine layers. The break falls where the names run out of room and the last line holds what is left. No option or control is stranded: a name is not something the reader is looking for in a particular place, and the layer's own count is in the header above. The alternative that fills every line — a fixed 118px track that each chip stretched into — made “Git”, fifteen pixels of text, sit in a 118px box, nearly seven times its own width, and turned a list of names into a table of identical boxes.
reasons.wrap|div.stack__head: The header carries three things: the layer's name, the gloss that explains it, and the number of tools under it. The name and the gloss are one phrase and now travel together; the count keeps the right-hand edge because nine counts in one column is worth aligning. Where the head is 288px the three need 298px, and the count takes a second line rather than the layer's name being broken in half — it is a figure, not an action, and it stays in the same right-hand column as every other layer's count. Before this the gloss was pushed to the far right of a 1018px track and landed under the count, 900px from the name it describes.
reasons.dead|span.stack__count: the stack layer head is one flex line: when the system name wraps internally (Thai text breaks within words), the label grows taller than the single-line count. The count stays on the bottom line, aligned with the label baseline - the space beneath it is the cost of keeping count and label on one line rather than letting count fall to its own line, which would make the wrap point shift between font loads.
reasons.dead|span.stack__role: the stack layer head is one flex line: when the system name wraps internally (Thai text breaks within words), the label grows taller than the single-line role. The role stays on the bottom line, aligned with the label baseline - the space beneath it is the cost of keeping role and count with the label on one line rather than letting them fall to their own lines, which would make the wrap point shift between font loads.
